newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Hall Kinion leaps at debut.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Hall Kinion leaps at debut.

text.p: Shares of Hall Kinion jumped more than 30 percent when they opened for trading on the Nasdaq on Tuesday after the company's initial public offering.
The stock was up to 20 in its first few minutes of trading from an IPO price of $15 a share.

The surge in the stock came even after underwriters priced the shares much higher than their original expectations. They filed first to sell shares for between $11 and $13 each, but bumped up the range to $14 to $15 each as orders piled in.

Hall Kinion, of San Jose, Calif., is a staffing company that specializes in information technology jobs. It provides computer whizzes like software developers, computer systems makers and telecommunications suppliers to companies including Microsoft Corp, Oracle Corp and Borland International Inc. No single client accounts for more than five percent of net revenues, it said in its prospectus.

About $33 million was raised in the IPO, but selling shareholders reaped about $13 million of the total, offering 848,333 of the total 2.515 million shares sold. Hall Kinion will use the proceeds to pay down debt, mostly from its 1996 acquisition of TeamAlliance, and possibly for acquisitions.
The Sprout Group, the venture capital arm of Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette, owns a stake in Hall Kinion.

The company was founded in December 1991 and has been profitable on a yearly basis since 1995. It is named after its chief executive, Brenda Hall, and former officer Todd Kinion, who is still on the board.
